The land of the petitioners which is the subject matter of the writ petition have been acquired for the purposes of Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board (for short 'KIADB') and a general award has been passed.

The petitioners have filed the instant writ petition with a prayer to set aside Lakshmamma vs The State Of Karnataka on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60422887/
2 the general award and make an award under the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text: However, in the course of the arguments, they submit that they would be satisfied if consent award as contemplated under Section 29(2) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966 (for short 'the Act') is passed.

2. The learned counsel appearing for the respondents submit that they have no objection to pass a consent award provided the petitioners produces all the relevant documents to show that they are the owner of the property.

Under similar circumstances, this Court in umpteen number of cases has permitted the land losers to claim compensation as per the consent award upon establishing the fact that they are the owners of the property.
There is no reason why a similar order should not be passed in the instant case also.
